facts: Photosynthesis is the process plants, algae and some bacteria use to turn light energy into chemical energy stored in sugar (glucose).
It uses carbon dioxide and water, and releases oxygen as a by-product.
The overall equation is 6CO2 + 6H2O + light energy -> C6H12O6 (glucose) + 6O2.
In plants it happens mainly in chloroplasts, which contain the green pigment chlorophyll.
It has two stages: the light-dependent reactions (in the thylakoid membranes) and the Calvin cycle (in the stroma).
Chlorophyll absorbs mostly red and blue light and reflects green light, which is why leaves look green.
Gravity is the force by which objects with mass attract each other.
Newton's law of universal gravitation says the force grows with the masses of the two objects and weakens with the square of the distance between them.
Near Earth's surface, a freely falling object accelerates at about 9.8 m/s^2 (ignoring air resistance).
Einstein's general theory of relativity describes gravity as mass and energy curving spacetime.
The Moon's surface gravity is about one-sixth of Earth's.
Gravity keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun, and the Moon's gravity is the main cause of ocean tides.
The solar system has eight planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
The Sun contains about 99.8% of the solar system's mass.
Jupiter is the largest planet.
Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, but Venus is the hottest because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat.
Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet by the International Astronomical Union in 2006.
Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
The water cycle is the continuous movement of water on, above and below Earth's surface.
Its main stages are evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection (runoff and soaking into the ground).
Transpiration is when plants release water vapour through their leaves.
Energy from the Sun drives evaporation.
About 97% of Earth's water is salt water in the oceans.
Clouds form when water vapour cools and condenses into tiny droplets around particles of dust.
The cell is the basic unit of life.
Prokaryotic cells, such as bacteria, have no nucleus; eukaryotic cells, such as plant, animal and fungal cells, do.
The nucleus contains the cell's DNA.
Mitochondria release energy from food through cellular respiration, producing ATP.
Plant cells have a cell wall and chloroplasts; animal cells do not.
The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.
The French Revolution began in 1789; the storming of the Bastille took place on 14 July 1789.
Its causes included a government financial crisis, food shortages, inequality between the three Estates, and Enlightenment ideas.
The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen was adopted in August 1789.
King Louis XVI was executed in January 1793.
The Reign of Terror (1793-1794) was led by the Committee of Public Safety, in which Robespierre was a leading figure.
The revolutionary period is usually said to end in 1799, when Napoleon Bonaparte took power in a coup.
